formulas.formula: Paid every fortnight? Budget every fortnight. Bills, savings and spending, sorted.
1. Setup: any one of your paydays, and when your year starts (1 July in Australia, 1 April in New Zealand).
2. Income and Bills: type each amount with how often it comes (weekly, monthly, quarterly...). Everything turns into a per-fortnight amount.
3. Savings Goals: what you're saving for. See how much to put away each fortnight.
4. Budget: plan your spending per fortnight. It shows what's left after bills and savings.
5. Transactions: log spending. Paying a bill? Use the Bills category. Moving money to savings? Use Savings.
6. Fortnightly and Dashboard: every pay period of the year (some years have 27!).
Transfer your Bills per fortnight into a separate bills account on payday. Bills are always covered.
Paid fortnightly? About every 11 years there are 27 paydays in a financial year. This sheet shows it.
Electricity and water come quarterly. Setting a little aside each fortnight smooths them out.
Your employer pays super (AU) or KiwiSaver (NZ). Extra contributions can be a savings goal.
Clear the white cells on Income, Bills, Budget, Transactions and Savings Goals, then update Setup.
Tinted cells: these calculate for you.
Green: on track, done, or money left.
Yellow: due this fortnight, or almost there.
Red: over budget, late, or something to check.
No worries. Your money's got a plan.
Set this up once. Everything else uses it.
Blank = 1 July (AU financial year). NZ: type 1 April.
One date you got paid. Blank = the year start.

Everything that comes in, after tax. Pick how often. It's converted to a per-fortnight amount.
Every bill with how often it comes and the next due date. Per Fortnight = what to move to your bills account each payday.
